subject: T423: multi-model whole-Bible chunking fork (experimental)
summary: Logos-scripture-graph is trying a speed fork: 4-5 AI models each run a continuous whole-Bible chunking marathon in separate scratch folders (M1_cursor..M5_composer_alt), starting from the same research baseline (literature types, grammar, Strong's G/H, wj/red-letter, observation substrate). After marathons: agreement spans = easy/consensus chunks; disagreement delta = governed focus queue. If fork fails, revert to T410 parallel_chunking_research_program baseline. Red-team pre-mortem required before marathons.

subject: T423 scratch-pad delta isolation pattern for hard corpus chunking
summary: T423 records a reusable scratch-pad acceleration idea: run several independent AI models over the same corpus with the same schema, rules, algorithms, literature hints, transparency sidecars, and non-authorizations, but require each model to make its own chunk-boundary judgments. Layer the resulting scratch chunk maps only after completion. Areas with little or no delta become higher-likelihood low-focus regions, still subject to risk sweeps for unanticipated high-risk literature forms. Areas with disagreement become the focus queue for Codex, Claude/frontier review, and owner-gated hard decisions. Theology should not be inserted into boundaries if avoidable; if a theological judgment or downstream theological risk is unavoidable, it must be made transparent, auditable, easy for future AI to spot, and marked non-authorizing.
method_steps: Give every model the same corpus rules, algorithms, schema, literature hints, and non-authorizations.
Run each model in an isolated scratch folder without reading other model outputs.
Require book strategy notes, confidence, low-confidence register, frontier escalation queue, and atlas candidate feed.
Batch-layer completed chunk maps only after models finish their own pass.
Treat low delta as a prioritization signal, not proof or authority.
Treat disagreement delta as the hard-focus queue for frontier review and owner-gated decisions.
Run risk sweeps for high-risk literature forms the original rules may have missed before any promotion.
purpose: Accelerate hard corpus chunking by using independent model agreement to reduce search space while preserving governance, auditability, and theological transparency.
known_limits: Agreement can hide shared blind spots if all models follow an incomplete template.
High-risk literature, apocalyptic, prophecy, poetry, doxology, discourse, textual variants, and unanticipated forms still require risk sweeps and frontier review.
Delta isolation does not itself decide correct chunk boundaries.
Template sameness must standardize fields and evidence logging, not force identical judgments.
